title: 2. Effects of dietary energy supplementation on growth, puberty attainment, and wool characteristics in growing ewe lambs fed medium-quality wheat forage.
content:
Abstract
The objective of this study was to evaluate effects of crude glycerin or corn supplementation at 5% dietary energy in a medium-quality wheat forage-based diet on growth performance, wool characteristics, and puberty attainment in Rambouillet ewe lambs. Twenty-four ewe lambs (32 ± 1 kg; 95 to 137 d of age) were stratified by body weight and birth type and randomly assigned to dietary treatments. Lambs received chopped wheat hay (CON; n = 8), chopped wheat hay supplemented with 5% crude glycerin on a DM basis (GLY; n = 8), or chopped wheat hay supplemented with 5% ground corn on DM basis (CORN; n = 8). Lambs were individually fed twice daily at 4% of body weight (BW) at initiation of the study, with orts collected daily and rations adjusted twice weekly based on feed refusals, allowing intake to reflect lamb appetite and assess observational palatability. Weekly BW measurements were recorded through d 63 and biweekly thereafter. Twice-weekly serum progesterone (P4) concentrations were used to assess pubertal status. Complete blood counts (CBC) were collected on d 0, 21, 42, and 63 to monitor immune and hematological responses. Wool fiber characteristics were evaluated by optical fiber diameter analysis at treatment initiation (d 0) and d 105, and wool growth was assessed by staple length measurement over the 105-d period. Ewe lamb BW increased over time but was not affected by dietary treatment (P = 0.51). Average daily gain from d 0 though d 161 did not differ among treatments (P = 0.49), averaging 0.08, 0.08, and 0.09 (± 0.01) kg/d for CON, GLY, and CORN lambs, respectively. Complete blood count parameters were largely stable across dietary treatments. Wool growth and fiber characteristics were unaffected by dietary treatment. Changes in staple length, mean fiber diameter, spin fineness, comfort factor, fiber curvature, and fiber diameter standard deviation did not differ among treatments (P > 0.10). However, uniformity of fiber diameter differed by treatment, with lambs receiving crude glycerin exhibiting greater fiber diameter variability compared with control and corn-fed lambs (P = 0.048). Puberty attainment was not affected by dietary treatment before onset of anestrous. Anestrus began on December 16, defined as the date when serum P4 concentrations fell below and remained below 1 ng/mL, when ewe body weights averaged 40.6 ± 1 kg. These results indicate that supplementing crude glycerin or corn to provide 5% of dietary energy did not improve growth performance, alter immune status, or accelerate puberty attainment prior to the onset of anestrous during the first year of life in ewe lambs fed medium-quality wheat forage.
